cards.front: What is skeletal muscle hypertrophy, and what primary net protein condition is required for its occurrence?
cards.back: Hypertrophy refers to the enlargement of muscle fiber cross-sectional area (CSA). It requires a net positive protein balance where muscle protein synthesis exceeds muscle protein degradation, resulting in the accretion of actin and myosin myofibrils.

cards.front: Which intracellular signaling pathway is activated by mechanical strain to directly stimulate muscle protein synthesis, and how does myostatin interact with muscle growth?
cards.back: Mechanical strain activates the Akt / mTOR pathway, which increases mRNA translation for contractile protein assembly. Concurrently, resistance exercise down-regulates myostatin (an inhibitory protein), removing molecular restraints on muscle growth.

cards.front: What is the typical time course for muscle protein synthesis elevation post-exercise, and how many workouts are required before structural hypertrophy is measurable?
cards.back: Muscle protein synthesis remains significantly elevated for up to 48 hours post-exercise. While early strength gains (weeks 1 to 4) stem from neural drive, structural hypertrophy requires a minimum of >16 consistent workouts before measurable increases in CSA occur.

cards.front: Contrast the primary loading variables used to maximize mechanical stress versus metabolic stress for muscle hypertrophy.
cards.back:
• Mechanical Stress: Heavy loads (>85% 1RM), high tension, eccentric focus, and long rest (2 to 5 minutes) to maximize high-threshold motor unit recruitment and Akt/mTOR activation.
  • Metabolic Stress: Moderate loads (60% to 75% 1RM), high volume (3–6 sets of 8–12 reps), and short rest (30 to 90 seconds) to drive metabolite accumulation (H+, lactate) and cell swelling.

cards.front: What is muscle fiber hyperplasia, and what is its contribution to total muscle enlargement in humans?
cards.back: Hyperplasia is an increase in total muscle fiber number via longitudinal fiber splitting. While verified in extreme animal overload models, hyperplasia contributes minimally (<10%) to total human muscle enlargement, with hypertrophy remaining the primary mechanism.

cards.front: Why do Type II fast-twitch muscle fibers manifest significantly greater cross-sectional area expansion than Type I slow-twitch fibers?
cards.back: Type II fibers possess higher myofibrillar protein packing density and exhibit significantly greater sensitivity to Akt/mTOR anabolic signaling under mechanical tension. Type I fiber growth is constrained by its endurance-oriented oxidative metabolic machinery.

cards.front: What is the main fast-twitch fiber type transition observed during chronic anaerobic training, and how rapidly does it occur?
cards.back: Pure Type IIx fibers shift toward Type IIa fibers along the myosin heavy chain (MHC) continuum (MHC IIx → MHC IIax → MHC IIa). Staron et al. (1990) showed significant Type IIx reductions after just 2 weeks (4 workouts) in females and 4 weeks (8 workouts) in males.

cards.front: What happens to fast-twitch fiber subtype proportions during periods of complete detraining or strategic competitive tapering?
cards.back: During detraining or tapering, Type IIa fibers revert back to Type IIx fibers, producing a temporary 'overshoot' where the percentage of pure, highly explosive Type IIx fibers temporarily exceeds pre-training baseline levels.

cards.front: How does an increased pennation angle following heavy resistance training affect muscle force production?
cards.back: An increased pennation angle allows a greater quantity of sarcomeres and myofibrils to be packed in parallel along the tendon. Although it slightly reduces the direct force vector per fiber, the massive gain in parallel contractile protein packing results in a net increase in maximal force and CSA.

cards.front: How does high-velocity sprint and plyometric training alter fascicle length, and what functional athletic advantage does this provide?
cards.back: Sprint and plyometric training increase muscle fascicle length by adding sarcomeres in series. This structural adaptation increases maximal muscle shortening velocity (Vmax), boosting explosive sprinting speed and rate of force development.

cards.front: Why do heavy-load powerlifters exhibit a decrease in mitochondrial and capillary density per unit muscle area?
cards.back: Heavy resistance hypertrophy causes a dilutional reduction: contractile protein accretion expands muscle fiber cross-sectional area disproportionately without a matching increase in organelle number, decreasing mitochondrial and capillary density per unit volume.

cards.front: What magnitude of phosphagen and glycogen supercompensation occurs in skeletal muscle following chronic resistance training?
cards.back: MacDougall et al. documented a 28% increase in resting creatine phosphate (CP) and an 18% increase in resting ATP after 5 months of resistance training. High-volume glycolytic training can increase resting muscle glycogen by up to 112%.
